title: Tanvi Patri, 15, wins India's first women's badminton medal at the Youth Olympics
dek: She took silver in Dakar after losing a three-game final to world junior champion Zhang Yi Xin, 26-24 in the decider.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Tanvi Patri won silver in the girls' singles at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, on Thursday, becoming the first Indian woman to win a badminton medal at the Games. The 15-year-old lost the final to China's Zhang Yi Xin, the reigning world junior champion, 21-15, 13-21, 24-26 in 1 hour 22 minutes, Khel Now and The Tribune reported.

Patri took the first game after recovering from 3-5 down with seven straight points. Zhang levelled after the interval in the second. In the decider Zhang led 19-10. Patri cut the gap to 19-15, then saved a run of match points to force extra points, and had three chances of her own to win gold before Zhang closed it out, according to Khel Now. Reports differ on whether she saved five or six match points.

India's previous individual badminton medals at the Youth Olympics were silvers for HS Prannoy in 2010 and Lakshya Sen in 2018. Sen also won gold in the mixed team event, in a team of players from eight countries.

The Badminton Association of India's general secretary called the result "an extraordinary accomplishment and a moment of immense pride for India", The Tribune reported.
